inputs.sbc_source: Equity-settled share award expense, cash-flow statement add-back: FY2025 RMB3.654m (1318.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:8466), H1 FY2026 RMB8.652m, H1 FY2025 RMB1.827m (1318.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt). No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). TTM to 30 Jun 2026 = 3.654 + 8.652 - 1.827 = 10.5m
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. Yahoo HKDCNY=X 0.8515 on 2026-10-16T09:03Z, i.e. 1 CNY = HK$1.1744 (fx_rate is CNY -> HKD, multiply CNY per-share values by it). No dual listing to parity-check; cross-check: HKD is pegged to USD at ~7.80 and USDCNY ~6.64 gives 6.64/7.80 = 0.851 CNY per HKD, consistent. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate - redo the rate if CNY moves more than ~2%.
inputs.fy0: TTM to 30 June 2026 (FY2025 + H1 FY2026 - H1 FY2025)
inputs.share_count_basis: 490,186,900 H shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim report, total share capital RMB245,093,450; all Unlisted Shares converted to H shares by 11 March 2026) plus 0.04m dilutive share awards (diluted WANOS 489,893,789 vs basic 489,852,380). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged; H1 FY2026 buyback of RMB26.9m funds the flat count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. China 10-year CGB ~1.8% + beta ~1.15 x China/HK equity risk premium ~6.5% = ~9.3%, rounded to 9.5%. All-equity capital structure (no borrowings) so WACC = cost of equity. No ad-hoc premium for key-person, single-brand or competition risk - those are charged in the scenarios and weights (risk charged once); same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal + interest, both on the cash-flow statement: FY2025 RMB41.3m + 2.3m = 43.7m = 0.87% of revenue; H1 FY2026 23.1m + 1.5m = 24.5m = 0.75%) is charged through lease_cost_pct_path at 0.9% of revenue (rising counter/flagship/HK footprint; lease liabilities grew 44m -> 91m over 18 months). Lease liabilities (RMB90.8m at 30 Jun 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (PPE depreciation + amortisation only: FY2025 48.1m = 0.95% of revenue). ebitda_margin_path is the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin (FY2025 33.7%, TTM 33.1%) so the lease charge is taken exactly once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (RMB4.7m balance, RMB1.1m H1 FY2026 profit share, <0.2% of profit). Not deducted; noted only.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: non-US operating consumer company -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations for currency, leases, SBC-near-zero). This is Mao Geping Cosmetics, a premium Chinese colour-cosmetics/skincare brand listed on HKEX in Dec 2024 - NOT Ping An Insurance (2318.HK); a prior folder mix-up has been corrected and no financial/insurer model applies. Base is TTM to 30 June 2026 so that the flows start after the balance-sheet date (no double count of H1 FY2026 cash already in net cash): revenue 5,050.5 + 3,267.3 - 2,588.2 = 5,729.5; reported FCF (OCF - PPE capex) 1,012.4 + 778.0 - 716.4 = 1,074.0; SBC 10.5; bank interest income 75.1 + 26.1 - 27.5 = 73.8 (stripped: net cash 3.7bn is ~3.7x the FCF base, so the cash pile is counted once, in the bridge). last_fcf = 1,074.0 - 10.5 - 73.8 = 989.7 per the house definition; after the 0.9% lease charge (treatment B) the lease-adjusted owner FCF is ~946m, 16.5% of TTM revenue, which is what the component build is anchored to. Net cash RMB3,659.4m = cash and equivalents 2,780.8 + time deposits 789.3 + wealth-management products at FVTPL 89.2 (30 Jun 2026 interim statement of financial position); restricted cash 2.2m excluded; no bank borrowings (the RMB320m FY2024 loan was repaid in H1 FY2025). Cash tax: PRC statutory 25% and the FY2025 effective rate is 25.0% (401.7/1,607.2); cash tax paid 23.9%; held at 25% throughout. Working capital: the business carries inventory (469+ SKUs) and counter receivables, and TTM OCF of 1,294m ran ~150m below net income + D&A, so growth consumes cash: wc_capture -10% of the revenue increase. Capex: FY2025 186m (3.7%) and H1 FY2026 120m (3.7%) are elevated by the Hangzhou in-house production facility (mid-2026 start) and R&D centre (end-2026); tapered to 2.0% mature with D&A ex-ROU rising from 0.95% to 1.5% as the factory depreciates. Historical note: the Metrics CSV FY2024 CapEx of 615.9m includes non-PPE investing outflows (the FY2025 annual shows FY2024 PPE purchases of 122.6m), so FY2024 reported FCF of 352.7m is understated on a like-for-like basis; the FY2025/TTM anchors use PPE purchases only. Street basis: SBC is ~0.2% of revenue, so house and street nearly coincide and band_position is close to degenerate; read it as 'SBC does not matter here'. Price is a regular close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: average of base-case years 1-5 revenue growth (22/17/13/10/8); historical equity and EPS CAGRs are unusable as growth proxies (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 60.3% (FY2022 1,134.5m -> FY2025 4,666.4m) is inflated by the Dec-2024 IPO proceeds, and EPS 3yr CAGR 11.8% (1.76 -> 2.46) is depressed by the share count going 200m -> 490m (pre-IPO capitalisation + IPO) while net income grew 3.4x (50.6% CAGR). Both diverge from revenue by far more than 30%; revenue and net-income growth are the usable series.
historical_growth.notes: Only four fiscal years of history (FY2022-FY2025; listed Dec 2024), so 5-year CAGRs are not available. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease cash, treatment B): FY2023 445.2m (495.0 - 0 - 19.8 - 30.0), FY2024 ~470m on a like-for-like PPE-capex basis (OCF 968.6 - PPE capex 122.6 - SBC 15.0 - interest 14.4 - leases 40.6 = 776m reported-basis; the CSV's 352.7m uses a 615.9m capex line that includes non-PPE outflows), FY2025 890.2m (1,012.4 - 3.7 - 75.1 - 43.7); FY2023->FY2025 owner-FCF CAGR 41.4% vs reported-FCF CAGR 43.0% - SBC is immaterial, the interest-income strip is the only meaningful adjustment and it grew with the IPO cash pile. Revenue growth is decelerating: FY2023 +57.8%, FY2024 +34.6%, FY2025 +30.0%, H1 FY2026 +26.2%.

base.growth_note: Y1 is the 12 months to Jun-2027: H2 FY2026 ~+25% (H1 ran +26.2% against a ~30% management target) fading to ~+20% in H1 FY2027, then a steady deceleration as the counter network (466 counters, 132 cities) saturates tier-1/2 cities and online growth normalises. Terminal 3% CNY: China premium beauty market forecast 4.0% CAGR to 2030 (Euromonitor, FY2025 AR) with a domestic-share tailwind, haircut for a single brand.
base.margin_note: Post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin drifts from TTM 33.1% (H1 FY2026 34.8% vs 36.4% a year earlier; selling expense 47.4% of revenue vs 45.2%) to 30% as advertising intensity stays high to defend premium positioning against Proya/Botanee premium lines (Morgan Stanley May-2026 margin cut). In-house factory COGS savings are assumed to be reinvested in marketing, not dropped through.

bull.narrative: Management's ~30% FY2026 target is roughly met (27%), fragrance and skincare scale as second and third legs, the Hong Kong counter/institute seeds a credible overseas channel, and the Hangzhou factory lifts gross margin enough to hold EBITDA margin at ~34% even with heavy marketing.

bear.narrative: Proya and Botanee premium sub-brands plus international houses discounting in China turn the RMB400-1,000 price band into a share fight; a weak Chinese consumer caps counter traffic; marketing spend rises faster than revenue and EBITDA margin settles at 25%. Growth stalls to ~2% by year 4 - a mature single-brand name with a founder-dependency discount. Note the bear case still generates positive owner FCF every year; it is a de-rating case, not a solvency case.

scenario_narratives.base: Mao Geping keeps compounding as the leading China-founded premium beauty brand, with revenue growth decelerating from the mid-20s to single digits over five years as counter expansion saturates and online growth normalises, while EBITDA margin drifts from 33% toward 30% because advertising intensity (selling expense already 47% of revenue) has to stay high against Proya/Botanee premium entrants - the H1 FY2026 pattern of profit growing slower than sales persists. Factory and R&D-centre capex rolls off after 2027, and the business remains a net-cash, ~25%-tax, SBC-free cash generator. The axes are (1) the rate of growth deceleration as the domestic premium segment matures and (2) whether marketing intensity stabilises or keeps rising.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's ~30% growth target is close to delivered in FY2026 and the deceleration is slower, carried by skincare and fragrance scaling as second and third categories, the membership base (22m+, 33% repurchase rate) lifting lifetime value, and a credible overseas start from the Harbour City counter and Hong Kong institute. The in-house Hangzhou factory lowers COGS enough to hold EBITDA margin at ~34% despite marketing spend. Terminal growth 3.5% and a 20x cap reflect a durable premium brand.
scenario_narratives.bear: The premium price band becomes contested as Proya, Botanee and discounting international houses converge on it, Chinese discretionary spending stays weak, and Mao Geping has to spend its way to flat share: EBITDA margin falls to 25% and growth stalls at ~2% from year 4. Founder/key-person and single-brand concentration cap any re-rating; terminal growth 2% and a 15x cap. Cash flow stays positive - the stock's 60% fall from its 52-week high is pricing something close to this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: single founder, single flagship brand, domestic rivals already launching premium lines at the same price points, and the H1 FY2026 margin compression is visible evidence rather than a hypothesis; the share price (down ~60% from the 52-week high) says the market is already partly there. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once - 30% growth sustained, factory margin gains dropping through, and an unproven overseas push. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the company on fully-taxed, lease-charged, SBC-charged, interest-stripped owner free cash flow in RMB, discounted at a CNY cost of equity, with the RMB3.7bn net cash added once in the bridge, then translated to HKD at the spot rate for comparison with the HKEX quote. The question the model is answering is how much growth deceleration and margin compression the de-rated price already discounts.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 1pp of permanent EBITDA margin is worth roughly 3% of the base value; the H1 FY2026 selling-expense ratio jump is the live datapoint.
Growth deceleration speed: the base assumes 22% fading to 8% by year 5; a faster fade toward the bear path halves the value.
Key-person and single-brand concentration: a reputational or succession event has no analogue in the driver paths beyond the bear weight.
CNY/HKD translation: a 5% RMB move shifts the HKD value 5% with no change in the business.
Platform concentration: half of product sales run through Tmall/Douyin/Xiaohongshu/JD, exposed to fee and algorithm changes.
Terminal value is the majority of EV in all scenarios; the Gordon value at 9.5%/3% (15.9x) sits below the 18x cap so the cap does not bind in the base case.
